title: Competitive sport
subtitle: beat, draw, champion, victory
summary: Talk about winning and losing, name the different kinds of competition, and understand the language of sports reports.

lesson.heading: Winning and losing
lesson.text: In football, the **score** is the number of goals a team has. You **win** a game and you **lose** a game, but you **beat** or **defeat** the other team. Note that you never 'win' a team.

examples.text: Spain played Poland and they **won** the game.

examples.note: spoken as 'one all'; also: It was a 1-1 draw.

left.label: score
left.text: Use score at any point in the game, including half-time.

right.label: result
right.text: The result is only the score at the end of the game.

lesson.heading: Competitions
lesson.text: A **competition** is an organised event in which people try to win something by being the best or the fastest. Individuals and teams **take part in** different types of competition.

examples.text: Tennis players and golfers **enter tournaments** such as the French Open.
Football and ice hockey teams play in **league** competitions, where they play against different teams.
Many teams also play in **cup** competitions, e.g. the FA Cup or the World Cup.
A cup competition ends with two teams playing against each other in a **final**.

lesson.note: Take part in means join with others in an activity.

lesson.heading: Winners and champions
lesson.text: The **winners** (opposite: the **losers**) are the **champions**. The **captain** is the leader of a team, and the competition itself may be called a **championship**.

examples.text: Philipp Lahm received the cup as **captain** of the winning team.
Kim Clijsters first won the **championship** in 2005.

lesson.heading: Words from sports reports
rows: run or swim faster than anyone in the world before
the time when you win a game or a competition
an important competition to decide who is the best
be in front of others during a competition
a competition in which people run, drive or swim

lesson.heading: Describing a great performance
lesson.text: **Superb**, **incredible** and **outstanding** all describe something or someone that is very good and of a very high quality. They are common in sports reports.

examples.text: It was one of the most **incredible** races of all time.
Bolt ran an **outstanding** time of 9.81 seconds and achieved a great **victory**.
She **gave up** tennis in 2007 to have a baby, and returned in 2009.

lesson.text: Learn the irregular forms together: win / won / won, lose / lost / lost, beat / beat / beaten, draw / drew / drawn.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with its past simple and past participle.
Choose the correct word: It was a fantastic ___ for the team - they won 4-0.
exercises.explanation: A victory is the time when you win a game or a competition.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: At half-time in the game, the ___ is 1-0 to Arsenal.
exercises.explanation: Result is only used at the end of the game; score can be used at any time.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct word: The French Open is a famous tennis ___.
exercises.explanation: Tennis players and golfers enter tournaments.

exercises.prompt: It was a good game but unfortunately we ___ 3-2.
exercises.explanation: You lose a game, but you beat the other team.

exercises.prompt: Holland ___ England 2-1, so they are in the semi-final.
exercises.explanation: You beat or defeat the other team - you never 'win' a team.
When both teams have the same score, they draw.

exercises.prompt: Carolina Kluft broke the heptathlon world ___ again last night.
exercises.explanation: You break a record when you do better than anyone in the world before.

exercises.prompt: There are 20 teams in the ___, and each team plays the other teams twice.
exercises.explanation: In a league competition every team plays against all the others.

exercises.prompt: Bradley Wiggins ___ part in the Tour de France in 2009 and finished fourth.
exercises.explanation: To take part in a competition means to join it with others.

exercises.prompt: I think Novak Djokovic is going to win. He's ___ 5-2 in the final set.
exercises.explanation: To lead means to be in front of the others during a competition.

exercises.prompt: Argentina are playing ___ Brazil next week.
Put each word into the right group.

exercises.statement: Croatia won Germany 3-2 in an exciting game.
exercises.explanation: Croatia beat Germany 3-2. You win a game, but you beat or defeat a team.

exercises.prompt: Report a drawn match between Spain and Italy.
exercises.answer: It was a 1-1 draw between Spain and Italy.
exercises.explanation: A 1-1 draw is spoken as 'one all'.
